title: The Back Door
hook: The old bus driver left one rule: if anything knocks on the back emergency door... don't stop, and don't look.
lines: I drive a school bus on a dark country route, long before the sun comes up.
The driver who had it before me left one rule, scratched into the sun visor.
If anything knocks on the back emergency door... don't stop. And don't look.
All fall, it was easy. Sleepy kids. Frosty fields. Twelve quiet stops.
Then one morning in December, out between the last farm and the river bridge...
three slow knocks... from the back of the bus.
Every kid went silent. Every single one.
I gripped the wheel, and kept my eyes on the road.
Three more knocks. Slower this time... patient.
Then nothing. Just the engine, and my own breathing, for miles.
At the school, the kids filed off like always, and I finally let go of the wheel.
Until the last little girl stopped on the steps... and looked back down the empty aisle.
'Mister,' she whispered. 'Why didn't you let him out?'
Behind me, very softly... three knocks. From the very back seat.
